articles.title: Why Are Wild Lynxes Giving Their Dinner a Bath?
articles.summary: Scientists caught Iberian lynxes dunking dead rabbits in water—a first for any meat-eating animal. Five female lynxes in Spain did this, maybe to help their cubs eat. It shows these rare cats can learn new tricks.

articles.title: This Tiny Knotted String Can Jump Higher Than Your House!
articles.summary: Scientists made a super-thin fiber that's tied in a knot. When heated, it suddenly unties and shoots almost 2 meters into the air—like a springtail bug. By changing the knot shape, they can make it flip or spin. It might help plant seeds in hard-to-reach places.

articles.title: How AI Is Learning to Be a Doctor's Best Helper
articles.summary: AI is popping up all over hospitals—reading X-rays, planning surgeries, even organizing schedules. But health care is super tricky, so developers need to work closely with doctors to make AI that's safe and truly helpful. More than 1,300 AI medical devices are already approved in the U.S.
